question: Find the values of 'a' and 'b' for which the system of equations 3x + y = 3 and (a - b)x + (a + b)y = 3a + b - 3 has infinite solutions.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a system to have infinite solutions, a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂

⇒ 3 / (a − b) = 1 / (a + b) = 3 / (3a + b − 3)

From 1st & 2nd terms: 3a + 3b = a − b ⇒ 2a = −4b ⇒ a = −2b

From 2nd & 3rd terms: 3a + b − 3 = 3a + 3b ⇒ 2b = −3 ⇒ b = −3/2

Substituting b into a: a = −2 × (−3/2) = 3

**∴ The correct answer is a = 3, b = −3/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

System of equations:

3x + y = 3

(a − b)x + (a + b)y = 3a + b − 3

**Formula Used:**

For a system of linear equations a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂ to have infinite solutions:

a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Comparing the given equations with standard form:

⇒ a₁ = 3, b₁ = 1, c₁ = 3

⇒ a₂ = a − b, b₂ = a + b, c₂ = 3a + b − 3

⇒ Applying the condition for infinite solutions:

⇒ 3 / (a − b) = 1 / (a + b) = 3 / (3a + b − 3)

Taking the first two parts of the equation:

⇒ 3 / (a − b) = 1 / (a + b)

⇒ 3(a + b) = 1(a − b)

⇒ 3a + 3b = a − b

⇒ 3a − a = −b − 3b

⇒ 2a = −4b

⇒ a = −2b --- (Equation 1)

Taking the second and third parts of the equation:

⇒ 1 / (a + b) = 3 / (3a + b − 3)

⇒ 1(3a + b − 3) = 3(a + b)

⇒ 3a + b − 3 = 3a + 3b

⇒ 3a − 3a − 3 = 3b − b

⇒ −3 = 2b

⇒ b = −3/2

Substitute the value of b in Equation 1:

⇒ a = −2 × (−3/2)

⇒ a = 3

**∴ The correct answer is a = 3, b = −3/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Condition for Unique Solution

A system of equations a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂ has a unique solution (intersecting lines) if a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂.

Condition for No Solution

A system of equations has no solution (parallel lines) if a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂.

Condition for Infinite Solutions

A system has infinitely many solutions (coincident lines) if a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.
